items.title: The Life-Changing Power of a Sabbatical
items.description:
It’s hard to focus on wellbeing when we’re expected to work nonstop until retirement. Taking a break from time to time should be a given, not a privilege.

Dr. Laurie works in one of the few industries that recognizes the importance of extended time off. As she begins her own year-long sabbatical from Yale, we’re revisiting her conversation with DJ DiDonna, author of Big Time Off, about what can happen when we step away from work for more than just a vacation.

DJ breaks down how to manage the biggest barriers to taking a sabbatical, from money and workplace optics to family responsibilities. He also explains why extended time off can help us recover from burnout, rethink our routines, and experiment with different versions of ourselves.

Whether you’re contemplating months away or just fantasizing about turning off your email, this episode makes the case that sometimes the best way to move forward is to stop for a while.

Experts Mentioned:

  • DJ DiDonna, Senior Lecturer of Business Administration at Harvard Business School

Resources Mentioned:

  • Big Time Off: The Transformative Power of Sabbaticals and How to Take One, by DJ DiDonna (2026)
  • Recover, Explore, Practice: The Transformative Potential of Sabbaticals, by Kira Schabram, Matt Bloom, and DJ DiDonna (Academy of Management Discoveries, 2023)
  • The Sabbatical Project

Related Episodes:

  • “You Can Change”
  • “Happiness Lessons of the Ancients: The Day of Rest”
  • “How to be Happier at Work (with Dan Harris)”
  • “Burnout and How to Avoid It”

items.title: You're Actually Not Bothering People Enough
items.description:
Most of us hate asking for favors. We worry about being a burden, coming across as needy, or facing rejection for asking too much. But what if our fear of bothering people is stopping us, and the people around us, from becoming happier?

Dr. Laurie explores why our instincts about asking for help are usually wrong. She speaks with psychologist Nicholas Epley about why asking others for help can actually make them like us more. And author and entrepreneur Jia Jiang shares how 100 days of asking for outlandish favors totally transformed his life.

Experts Mentioned:

  • Nicholas Epley, Professor of Behavioral Science at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business
  • Jia Jiang, author, entrepreneur, and expert in “rejection therapy”

Resources Mentioned:

  • Rejection Proof: How I Beat Fear and Became Invincible Through 100 Days of Rejection, by Jia Jiang (2015)
  • “What I Learned from 100 Days of Rejection,” by Jia Jiang (TED, 2016)
  • “100 Days of Rejection Therapy,” by Jia Jiang (YouTube series, 2013)
  • RejectionTherapy.com
  • “Surprisingly Happy to Have Helped: Underestimating Prosociality Creates a Misplaced Barrier to Asking for Help,” by Xuan Zhao and Nicholas Epley (Psychological Science, 2022)
  • “Beautiful mess effect: Self–other differences in evaluation of showing vulnerability,” by Anna Bruk, Sabine Scholl, and Herbert Bless (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 2018)

Related Episodes:

  • “Treating the Pain of a Broken Heart”
  • “Forget Small Talk: Go Deep Instead”
  • “The Surprising Case for Oversharing”
